tips.title: Cut cards from the back
tips.content: Cut duplex card sheets from the back, if fronts and backs are misaligned it won't be obvious from the card backs and the cards will still be playable.

tips.title: Laminate twice
tips.content: If your laminated PnP cards are splitting open at the edges, consider passing them through the laminator a second time.

tips.title: Use a higher heat setting
tips.content: If your cards are delaminating at the 3mil heat setting, try passing them through at the 5mil heat setting on your laminator.

tips.title: Rotary cutter + metal blade
tips.content: Rotary cutter + metal blade. Highly precise cuts once you get it. A bit muscle-taxing, however, if you use thick laminated paper!

tips.title: Ink tank printers
tips.content: Ink tank printers can work wonders: my Canon Pixma has printed A LOT, with high quality, and still has half ink left over!

tips.title: Learn a design tool
tips.content: Inkscape (and other free design tools) is your friend. Learn a program, and the quality of your designs will increase substantially.

tips.title: Sleeve laminated cards
tips.content: Laminating and corner-rounding a card, and then sleeving it, will get you a premium feeling. The thickness of a pnp'd laminated card in ~140 mg paper is just right.

tips.title: Get an ink tank printer
tips.content: Get an ink tank printer. It's more expensive up front but cheaper in the long run.

tips.title: Use coin capsules for circle tokens
tips.content: Punch out 1-inch circle tokens and place them inside 25mm plastic coin capsules for easy yet deluxe circle tokens.

tips.title: Peeling off sticker backs
tips.content: Sometimes using another scrap piece of sticker on the back of the first will peel the backing off.

tips.title: Just do it
tips.content: Don't overthink. I spent so long early on wanting to have the smoothest process, finding the "perfect" way to craft, that I often just never started.

tips.title: Experiment
tips.content: Don't be afraid to try different techniques and experiment to find what works for you.

tips.title: Play test first
tips.content: Play test a game first to see if you like it before fully investing time and money into crafting a "forever copy".

tips.title: Start small
tips.content: Start small with your first project so you can get a handle on how to do things. Work up to larger projects if you have any in mind.

tips.title: Choose your cutter
tips.content: Find what cutting method works for you (mine is a guillotine cutter) and use it.

tips.title: Paper and card sleeves
tips.content: 200+gsm paper and card sleeves are a great way to start.

tips.title: Eco-tank printer
tips.content: Buy an eco-tank inkjet printer, and print frequently so the nozzles don't clog.

tips.title: Test print
tips.content: Test Print One Page before printing out 300.

tips.title: Don't rush
tips.content: TAKE YOUR TIME, don't rush.

tips.title: Digital rules
tips.content: If you like digital copies of rules, get a comics app for your tablet and copy the rules PDF to the tablet instead of printing it out.

tips.title: Card backing
tips.content: Use construction paper or print card backs to make cards less flimsy.

tips.title: Thicker tokens
tips.content: Use coin protectors or glue onto pennies to make circular tokens.

tips.title: Explore your creativity
tips.content: You can create whatever you want. Create your own game, modify a game you already own, create something like a game that already exists from scratch. The only limit is your imagination.

tips.title: Practice first
tips.content: You don't have to do a full board game on your first try. Create some extra pieces or cards for a game you already know with some fan expansions or official PNP extra components so you can practice.

tips.title: Half full printer tray
tips.content: Make sure your paper drawer is at least half full, this really makes a difference when printing (manual) duplex

tips.title: Edit PDFs
tips.content: Affinity (software, free version) is capable of editing PDF files. For example, to remove cut lines or extract images.

tips.title: Dry erase pocket sleeves
tips.content: You don't need to laminate all your Roll and Writes. There exist Dry Erase Pocket Sleeves that can hold your paper and make it reusable.

tips.title: Reuse old boxes
tips.content: reuse old boxes for storing pnp games. You can print on full page label paper to cover the full box and make it look amazing. Add a layer of cold laminate over it to make it even better.

tips.title: Don't cut to the edge
tips.content: Don't cut to the edge of the sheet, to keep the crop marks in place.

tips.title: Use permanent markers
tips.content: Using permanent markers on matte laminated roll and write sheets requires tedious alcohol wiping to clean between games. Try wet-erase markers on matte laminate and rinse the sheets easily under running water!

tips.title: Start small and simple
tips.content: Start with a small game. It can be an 18 card game like Rove, Mini Rogue, or Galdor's Grip. Just use printer paper and a deck of playing cards. Packing tape the front and backs. That way you don't have to fuss about the fronts and backs aligning properly.

builds.title: Sole Survivor
builds.blurb: New PnP finished today. This is a preview of "Sole Survivor". Very excited to see how this plays as I was part of the play testing back in December. All components laminated. Lego pieces for xenomorphs, player and transporter modules. Two d6 for health and action points. For the play testing version, I mounted the boards on cardboard. Now the boards are laminated, they may too slippery. Hopefully the weight of the Lego will help as I used plastic cubes previously.

contests.title: 2026 1-Card Print and Play Contest
contests.description: Design a complete game that fits on a single card — front and back. One card, one page of rules. Contest ends July 31, 2026.

contests.title: 2026 Bad Comet Cozy Game Design Contest
contests.description: Design a cozy game for the Bad Comet Cozy Game Design Contest. Contest ends August 31, 2026.

contests.title: 2026 9-Card Nanogame PnP Design Contest
contests.description: Create a new solo, co-op, or competitive game that fits on one sheet of 9 poker-size cards (2.5" x 3.5") plus rules pages, using up to 24 generic components total or none at all. Contest ends May 31, 2026.

contests.title: 2026 Two-Player PnP Game Design Contest
contests.description: Let's play some inexpensive and innovative two-player games! With this contest, we hope to encourage designers to create interesting new gaming experiences specifically for a pair of gamers. Contest ends May 31, 2026.

contests.title: 2026 Deck Hand Games Design Contest
contests.description: The Challenge: To make an 18-card game that works in conjunction with any standard deck of playing cards. Deadline: June 26, 2026

contests.title: 2026 Solomode Contest
contests.description: Design a solo mode for a game that does not have one, or has one that you find lacking. Contest ends June 30, 2026.

contests.title: 2026 Children & Family Game Design Contest
contests.description: This contest is meant to design games that we can play with the children, or games that children can play together. The focus should be on games that children (9 and under) can play with their families. Voting closes May 15, 2026

contests.title: 2026 Print and Play Wargame Design Contest
contests.description: Games entered in this contest should be purpose-designed wargames. Games may be solo, two player, multi-player or even co-operative. However it is critical that the game is a wargame. The primary focus should therefore be on conflict and warfare.

wips.title: Stone Skipping
wips.description: A cozy 1-4 player card game where you skip stones across the beach to earn coins and build chains. Flip cards, hit other stones to rocket forward, and buy special cards from a market to push further. Four rounds, most points wins.

wips.title: Mountain of Perils
wips.description: A one-card hex dungeon crawl as a mountain exploration with perils, treasures, and fights. Quick to set up and play in short moments — perfect for a job pause or waiting in an office. One or two players, 30 minutes, 10 d6 and 10 cubes.

wips.title: Zeus
wips.description: A quick 1-player dice manipulation game. Three dice circle a track — each turn select one die and move all dice for its pips. Each die triggers the icon's effect where it stops. Use your thunderbolts wisely to manipulate the dice. 5-10 minutes.

wips.title: Clouds of War
wips.description: A solo Great War aerial wargame confined in 54 cards and one A4 page. Pilot through Patrol, Escort, and Balloon Busting missions over a French battlefield. Moderate damage system and dogfight mechanics combined with various in-air events provide just enough randomness and replayability for a compelling narrative. Your pilot gains better traits as they progress, increasing survivability in the skies.

wips.title: DOKUSU
wips.description: DOKUSU is a SUDOKU-inspired puzzle in 9 cards. Arrange the nine cards into a 9x9 grid so that no number repeats in any one column or row, or within any of the nine 3x3 sub-grids.

wips.title: Crafting Crawler
wips.description: A dungeon-building and exploration game where you generate the map as you forge your path, defeating the threats that lie within. Choose your hero (or a party of adventurers) to reach the deepest corners of this ever-shifting dungeon. Defeat the Ancient Dragon and claim the riches hidden behind its walls.

wips.title: The Test of Time
wips.description: Test of Time is a solo 9 card civilization game. From the dawn of time to the modern day, you will guide a small tribe of hunter-gatherers into a mighty empire, by managing and growing the population, using and developing new technologies, managing resources, developing theories of government, constructing a mighty wonder of the world, doing battle with a rival nation, surviving four historical ages, and developing enough culture to become a nation that stands the Test of Time.

wips.title: 1st Hero
wips.description: In this world, you do not merely fight; you lead. As a legendary Guild Master, your path is carved through untamed wilds and the remains of fallen kings. But steel alone will not win this war. Here, the clash of blades is replaced by the cunning of the mind.

wips.title: Doodle Bash
wips.description: In Doodle Bash you'll level up your doodling skills by combining simple shapes into an astonishing variety of clever drawings. Arrange your doodles in a pleasing way to score big and just maybe you'll be an artist some day! Doodle Bash is a 1-page, app-assisted PnP game. It was my entry in the 2025 Roll and Write contest where it placed 2nd overall.

wips.title: Flipping Little Dinos
wips.description: Flipping Little Dinos is a fast paced little puzzle. Players compete by placing Dinosaurs on a shared ecosystem with four different dinosaur species and four different ways to score. Score the most points with the dinosaurs you draw or flip them!

wips.title: THE WORST PART OF BEING CAUGHT IN A TIME LOOP
wips.description: You are agents of the Temporal Research Division, racing across a 3×3 grid to collect four anomaly Relics before the timeline collapses. Every failed loop leaves the board scarred and your time shorter, but the Relics make your team stronger with each attempt. A coop puzzle of movement prediction, edge-color matching, and cascading grid shifts — playable solo or with up to four agents.
